newsitem.title: USA: Hilton threatens possible ITT terms change.
newsitem.headline: Hilton threatens possible ITT terms change.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp on Tuesday repeated its desire to meet with ITT Corp to discuss its $55 per share bid for ITT, but it said if ITT took measures to reduce a merger's value, Hilton might "adjust the terms" of its offer.

"We do not intend to be deterred from pursuing our offer by any actions that you may choose to take," Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach wrote in a February 11 letter to ITT Chairman Rand Araskog.
"To the extent your actions reduce the value of the combination to us, we would, of course, be required to review the per share price that we would be able to pay," Bollenbach added.
In its initial bid on January 27, Hilton also said it might consider raising the offer after a review of ITT's books.
In the letter, Bollenbach called the initial response to Hilton's acquisition offer "overwhelmingly positive" from company shareholders and financial analysts.
Hilton also named 25 potential candidates for ITT's board of directors should its $6.5 billion bid for ITT come down to a battle for control of ITT's board.

Hilton's proposed slate of board members includes a mix of businessmen and women from the hospitality and gambling industries, as well as private investors and a former governor of New Jersey, James Florio.

In a statement, Hilton said 11 of the individuals would be named to a slate of candidates for ITT's current board seats, and the other 14 could be added if ITT attempted to thwart Hilton's bid by boosting the number of board members.
A spokesman for ITT declined to comment.
ITT has not yet scheduled its next annual shareholder meeting, but it normally holds the gathering in mid-May.
ITT's board met on February 4th and discussed the Hilton offer, but ITT did not make a public response to the proposal after the board meeting. It has until Feb. 14 to respond.
The Hilton list of 25 nominees is comprised of:
1) Daniel J. Altobello - Potomac, Md. - chairman of the board of ONEX Food Services Inc and former chairman of the board, president and chief executive officer of Caterair International Corp.
2) George N. Aronoff - Cleveland, Ohio - partner, law firm of Benesch, Friedlander, Coplan & Aronoff.
3) Scott H. Bice - Pasadena, Calif. - Dean, University of Southern California Law School.
4) Barrie K. Brunet - Reno - former director and executive officer of Bally's Grand Inc.

5) Henry A. Collins - Bernardsville, N.J. - managing director and portfolio manager, Barrett Associates Inc., investment managers. Former director and senior vice president of Kidder Peabody, responsible for Equity Research and Institutional Equity Sales.
6) John Danhakl - Los Angeles - partner, Leonard Green & Partners, a private merchant banking firm.

7) Ernest E. East - Oro Valley, Ariz. - vice president, corporate secretary and general counsel, Artisoft Inc and former vice president and general counsel of Elsinore Corp; former vice president of Taj Mahal, Trump Plaza and Trump's Castle Casinos.
8) James J. Florio - Piscataway, N.J. - partner, law firm of Florio & Perrucci, P.C.; former governor of New Jersey.
9) Fred D. Gibson, Jr. - Las Vegas - chairman, president and chief executive officer of American Pacific Corp.
10) John E. Humphreville - Los Angeles - private investor.
11) Dianne Jett - Las Vegas - former president, Sprint-Central Telephone Co of Nevada.
12) Robert L. Johander - Eden Prairie, Minn. - chairman and chief executive officer of ValueVision International Inc.
13) Russell D. Jones - Los Angeles - vice president, Sonnenblick-Goldman Co., real estate investment bankers.
14) Robert S. Kingsley - Far Hills, N.J. - private investor, former president and chief operating officer, HFS Gaming Corp. and former president and COO of Caesars World Resorts Inc.
